ask-me-no-questions.summary: Laura and Barty are sent away to escape a deadly epidemic and end up at their aunt's unsettling home. The aunt is cold toward them, and strange events hint at dark secrets that the siblings try to uncover.
ask-me-no-questions.title: Ask Me No Questions

at-the-mouth-of-the-luckiest-river.note: Plot description is the one-line library summary only.
at-the-mouth-of-the-luckiest-river.summary: A young Athabascan boy in Alaska stands up to his tribe's medicine man to try to head off a conflict with a neighboring Eskimo people. It is a short children's story set along a river.
at-the-mouth-of-the-luckiest-river.title: At the Mouth of the Luckiest River

away-goes-sally.note: Plot sketch comes from library catalog text in search results; character names Sally Pickering and Uncle Jotham from the earlier draft could not be verified and were removed.
away-goes-sally.setting: New England, a journey from Massachusetts to Maine
away-goes-sally.summary: Sally and her relatives set out on a winter journey from Massachusetts to Maine in a small house mounted on runners. It is the first of five historical novels about Sally.
away-goes-sally.title: Away Goes Sally

characters: Maa — an ewe who teaches Babe about sheep
babe-the-gallant-pig.note: First published in Britain as The Sheep-Pig (Gollancz, 12 Nov 1983); US edition (Crown, 1985) titled Babe: The Gallant Pig.
babe-the-gallant-pig.summary: A piglet won at a fair is meant for the Christmas table but is taken under the wing of the sheepdog Fly. He learns to herd sheep by asking them politely rather than bossing them. His talent leads to the sheepdog trials.
babe-the-gallant-pig.title: Babe: The Gallant Pig

characters: The Beast — master of the enchanted castle
Roderick Huston — her father, a ruined merchant
beauty-a-retelling-of-the-story-of-beaut.note: Added Phoenix Award honor; named father and sisters; setting is Blue Hill and the castle. Reading age not stated by source; set null.
beauty-a-retelling-of-the-story-of-beaut.setting: A small town called Blue Hill, and an enchanted castle in the woods
beauty-a-retelling-of-the-story-of-beaut.summary: Honour, nicknamed Beauty, is the plain, bookish daughter of a merchant whose fortunes have collapsed. When her father stumbles on an enchanted castle, she volunteers to live there with its Beast, and an unexpected friendship grows. It was McKinley's first novel.
beauty-a-retelling-of-the-story-of-beaut.title: Beauty: A Retelling of the Story of Beauty and the Beast

beezus-and-ramona.summary: Beatrice, nicknamed Beezus, finds her wildly imaginative little sister Ramona a trial, from library mishaps to a birthday party. It is a funny, honest look at sisterly frustration and love.
beezus-and-ramona.title: Beezus and Ramona

better-known-as-johnny-appleseed.setting: Early American frontier, Ohio River country
better-known-as-johnny-appleseed.summary: The life and legend of John Chapman told in nine stories, each named for a kind of apple. They follow his travels west from the Youghiogheny River to the Mississippi.
better-known-as-johnny-appleseed.title: Better Known as Johnny Appleseed

black-beauty.summary: A horse tells his life story, from kind masters to cruel ones, in a plea for compassion toward animals.
black-beauty.title: Black Beauty

black-gold.note: Described as a fictionalized true story, not strict nonfiction. Publisher Rand McNally per library catalogs. Wikipedia lists a Sequoyah Book Award (1960).
black-gold.summary: A fictionalized account of the real horse Black Gold, who won the 1924 Kentucky Derby. The story follows the horse with his trainer Hanley Webb and jockey Jaydee Mooney.
black-gold.title: Black Gold

black-hearts-in-battersea.summary: Simon travels to London to study painting and finds a plot against the Duke of Battersea. With the help of the streetwise Dido Twite he chases through rooftops and rivers.
black-hearts-in-battersea.title: Black Hearts in Battersea

black-suits-from-outer-space.note: Draft setting 'small American town' was not confirmed and is left blank.
black-suits-from-outer-space.series: Black Suits from Outer Space #1 (followed by The Dandelion Caper, 1986, and The Calvin Nullifier, 1987)
black-suits-from-outer-space.summary: Teenagers Calvin and Kathy are puzzled by repeated visits from mysterious men in black suits. They end up hiding a huge hairy alien from the school principal and the police chief.
black-suits-from-outer-space.title: Black Suits from Outer Space

bleak-house.summary: A never-ending lawsuit entangles many lives in Victorian London. Orphan Esther Summerson, her guardian and a web of secrets are drawn together.
bleak-house.title: Bleak House

blue-heron.note: Setting corrected from Maine to Massachusetts shore (per library summaries found via search; the fetched Open Library record confirms 1992, Avi, subjects family problems/herons/friendship). Decade of setting not verified.
blue-heron.setting: Massachusetts seashore, a summer in the 1980s
blue-heron.summary: Almost-thirteen-year-old Maggie spends August at the shore with her father, stepmother and their new baby, and feels like an outsider. Watching a great blue heron gives her something of her own while her family strains.
blue-heron.title: Blue Heron

blue-willow.summary: Janey is the daughter of migrant workers during the Great Depression. She hopes to hold on to a blue willow plate and find a permanent home.
blue-willow.title: Blue Willow

boy-tales-of-childhood.setting: Wales, England and Norway, 1916 to the 1930s
boy-tales-of-childhood.summary: Roald Dahl's memoir of his early years, from family holidays in Norway to miserable boarding schools. It shows the events that later turned up in his stories.
boy-tales-of-childhood.title: Boy: Tales of Childhood

characters: Jess (Jesse) Aarons — fearful boy who draws
May Belle Aarons — Jess's little sister
bridge-to-terabithia.note: Added illustrator Donna Diamond; setting Lark Creek, VA.
bridge-to-terabithia.summary: Jess Aarons, a fifth-grader who secretly loves to draw, becomes friends with new neighbor Leslie Burke. Together they invent Terabithia, a secret kingdom in the woods. The friendship changes how Jess faces his world, and the book deals with imagination and grief.
bridge-to-terabithia.title: Bridge to Terabithia

brighty-of-the-grand-canyon.summary: Brighty, a wild burro, roams the Grand Canyon and befriends prospector Old Timer. Based on a real burro, he helps protect a friend from a thief.
brighty-of-the-grand-canyon.title: Brighty of the Grand Canyon

bunnicula-a-rabbit-tale-of-mystery.summary: The Monroe family's cat Chester becomes convinced that their new pet rabbit is a vampire. The family dog Harold narrates their funny investigation.
bunnicula-a-rabbit-tale-of-mystery.title: Bunnicula: A Rabbit-Tale of Mystery

caddie-woodlawn.summary: Eleven-year-old Caddie is a tomboy on the Wisconsin frontier who prefers running wild with her brothers to learning ladylike ways. Based on the author's grandmother's childhood.
caddie-woodlawn.title: Caddie Woodlawn

calico-captive.summary: In 1754, Miriam Willard and her family are captured in a raid by Abenaki and taken to Canada. Based on a true story, it follows her struggle to keep hope.
calico-captive.title: Calico Captive

call-it-courage.summary: A Polynesian boy afraid of the sea sets out alone in a canoe to prove himself. He lands on an island and faces danger.
call-it-courage.title: Call It Courage

cannery-row.summary: A kind marine biologist and a crowd of down-on-their-luck neighbors share life along a sardine-cannery street. When they plan a party for Doc, things go happily wrong.
cannery-row.title: Cannery Row

characters: Margaret Mary — friend from a proper household
Uncle Hat — relative who talks in numbers and rhymes
Cousin Coralee — feathered relative with a baby
cassie-binegar.summary: Cassie's family moves to a shore house near her father's and brothers' fishing boat, and she misses having a space of her own. She also feels guilty over her grandfather's death after she once yelled at him. Over the story she learns to accept imperfection and change in herself and her eccentric family.
cassie-binegar.title: Cassie Binegar

cat-running.summary: Cat, a tomboy in a Dust Bowl migrant camp, befriends a teacher and a family of Okies facing prejudice. She learns about courage and fairness.
cat-running.title: Cat Running

characters: Cat — a young farm cat in search of a name
cat-walk.note: Corrected: this is a farm cat on a quest, not a stray in an American town; Harper & Row, 1983.
cat-walk.setting: A farm and the road beyond
cat-walk.summary: A young barnyard cat who wants more than a life of catching rats sets out in search of a name. His journey eventually leads him to a place he can call home.
cat-walk.title: Cat Walk

catherine-called-birdy.summary: Fourteen-year-old Catherine, nicknamed Birdy, keeps a diary in 1290s England while dodging unwanted suitors arranged by her father. Funny, sharp and surprisingly modern.
catherine-called-birdy.title: Catherine, Called Birdy

characters: Thelma, Roger, James and Harriet — winged kittens
catwings.summary: Four winged kittens leave their city alley to find a safe home in the countryside, where they meet a kind pair of children.
catwings.title: Catwings

characters: Charlie Bucket — kind, poor, hopeful boy
charlie-and-the-chocolate-factory.setting: An English town and Wonka's fantastical factory, mid-20th century
charlie-and-the-chocolate-factory.summary: Poor Charlie Bucket wins a golden ticket to tour the mysterious chocolate factory of Willy Wonka. Four other children with very bad habits come along, and the factory holds surprises for each of them.
charlie-and-the-chocolate-factory.title: Charlie and the Chocolate Factory

characters: President of the United States — flustered leader
charlie-and-the-great-glass-elevator.setting: Wonka's factory, outer space, and a space hotel
charlie-and-the-great-glass-elevator.summary: The glass elevator shoots out of the chocolate factory and into outer space, with Charlie's whole family aboard. They meet strange visitors and an astronaut crisis before heading home.
charlie-and-the-great-glass-elevator.title: Charlie and the Great Glass Elevator

characters: Fern Arable — girl who saves Wilbur
charlotte-s-web.setting: A New England farm, mid-20th century
charlotte-s-web.summary: Wilbur the pig is saved from slaughter by his friend Charlotte, a barn spider, who weaves words into her web to convince the farmer. It is about friendship and the cycle of life.
charlotte-s-web.title: Charlotte's Web

cheetah.note: Open Library dates Arnold's Cheetah to 1989; a separate record credits Richard Hewett on a 1992 edition. The photographer credit comes from a LibraryThing listing.
cheetah.summary: A children's nonfiction look at the physical features, habits and life cycle of cheetahs, both wild and in zoos.
cheetah.title: Cheetah

children-of-the-wolf.note: Published by Viking Press (per library record).
children-of-the-wolf.summary: In an Indian orphanage in 1920, a clergyman and two boys capture two girls found living with wolves. Fourteen-year-old Mohandas is asked to teach them to walk and talk, and he struggles with the adults' motives.
children-of-the-wolf.title: Children of the Wolf

crash.summary: Crash Coogan is a brash, football-obsessed seventh grader whose friendship with a gentle Quaker neighbor challenges him. When his grandfather is ill he grows.
crash.title: Crash

danny-dunn-and-the-anti-gravity-paint.setting: A town in the United States, 1950s
danny-dunn-and-the-anti-gravity-paint.summary: Danny Dunn and his friends discover a paint that defies gravity and have a flying adventure that goes wonderfully wrong. A science-minded romp for young readers.
danny-dunn-and-the-anti-gravity-paint.title: Danny Dunn and the Anti-Gravity Paint

danny-the-champion-of-the-world.summary: Danny lives with his devoted father in a caravan next to a filling station. When he discovers his dad's secret nighttime hobby, the two plan a grand scheme against a snobbish landowner.
danny-the-champion-of-the-world.title: Danny the Champion of the World

characters: Wilkins Micawber — cheerful, always in debt
david-copperfield.note: Notebook edition is an adaptation by Gertrude Moderow (Open Library lists a Scott, Foresman David Copperfield, 1951, by her); the original novel appeared 1849-50. Adaptation details not otherwise verified.
david-copperfield.setting: Victorian England: Suffolk, Yarmouth, London, Dover, Canterbury
david-copperfield.summary: Dickens's novel follows David from a lonely childhood through cruel stepparents, boarding school and factory work to a writing career. Along the way he meets the Micawbers, his great-aunt Betsey Trotwood, Steerforth and Uriah Heep.
david-copperfield.title: David Copperfield

dicey-s-song.summary: Dicey Tillerman and her siblings settle with their grandmother after being abandoned. They learn to belong.
dicey-s-song.title: Dicey's Song

dinosaur-mountain-graveyard-of-the-past.illustrator: Richard Hewett (photographs; catalogs differ on his credit)
dinosaur-mountain-graveyard-of-the-past.note: Clarion Books, 1989, 48 pages (from catalog records). Draft 'Paleontologists' character tag dropped.
dinosaur-mountain-graveyard-of-the-past.setting: Dinosaur National Monument, Utah and Colorado
dinosaur-mountain-graveyard-of-the-past.summary: A children's nonfiction book about the fossils found at Dinosaur National Monument and what they have taught scientists about dinosaurs. It describes how bones were found in a Utah sandstone ridge in 1909.
dinosaur-mountain-graveyard-of-the-past.title: Dinosaur Mountain: Graveyard of the Past

dinosaurs-down-under-and-other-fossils-f.identified: Clarion Books, 1990 (Open Library). Photographer credit and plot come from a library catalog record seen in search results; the catalog page itself could not be opened. Open Library also lists a 1994 edition.
dinosaurs-down-under-and-other-fossils-f.summary: A photo-illustrated look at how an exhibit of Australian fossils was shipped to a Los Angeles museum, put together and put on display. It introduces the unusual prehistoric animals of Australia along the way.
dinosaurs-down-under-and-other-fossils-f.title: Dinosaurs Down Under: And Other Fossils from Australia

characters: Rat and Mouse Club — storytelling rodents
doctor-dolittle-s-zoo.note: Corrected series position: fifth Dolittle book, not sixth. Earlier characters Polynesia, Jip and Dab-Dab were not confirmed for this volume.
doctor-dolittle-s-zoo.summary: Doctor Dolittle comes home from his voyages and sets his house in order, expanding his cage-free zoo with a home for crossbred dogs and a club for rodents. Much of the book is the members of the Rat and Mouse Club telling their life stories, and the Doctor also helps Kling, the Dog Detective, with a mystery.
doctor-dolittle-s-zoo.title: Doctor Dolittle's Zoo

dominic.summary: A cheerful dog sets off to see the world, meeting oddball characters. A weasel-like villain stands in his way.
dominic.title: Dominic

characters: The drummer boy from the past
earthfasts.note: published_last 2000 = Candlefasts. Wikipedia's Earthfasts page is a disambiguation; used the Mayne page plus search results. Summary corrected to the time-slip plot. Setting only loosely sourced (Mayne lived in North Yorkshire); character name 'Nowt' not confirmed, removed.
earthfasts.summary: A drummer boy from the eighteenth century goes into a cave looking for Arthur's treasure and comes out two centuries later. Modern schoolboys David and Keith befriend him, and old magic breaks into the present. It opens a trilogy that draws on the King Arthur legend.
earthfasts.title: Earthfasts

characters: Cal and Aron Trask — their twin sons
east-of-eden.note: Source corrected to the novel article. Added Cathy and Aron; no awards listed.
east-of-eden.summary: Two families, the Trasks and the Hamiltons, settle California's Salinas Valley and live out an echo of Cain and Abel across generations. The book asks how far people are free to choose who they become.
east-of-eden.title: East of Eden

eight-mules-from-monterey.note: Morrow, 1982 (Open Library and a library catalog). Wikipedia's Beatty page lists 1966, which conflicts with those sources.
eight-mules-from-monterey.summary: In the summer of 1916 a thirteen-year-old girl and her brother go with their widowed mother on a mule trip into the California mountains. Their mother is setting up library outposts in remote communities.
eight-mules-from-monterey.title: Eight Mules from Monterey

emily-s-runaway-imagination.summary: Emily, a girl in a small Oregon farm town in the 1920s, has a big imagination that gets her into scrapes. She wants a library for the town and works hard to see it built.
emily-s-runaway-imagination.title: Emily's Runaway Imagination

encyclopedia-brown-and-the-case-of-the-m.summary: Boy detective Encyclopedia Brown solves ten short mysteries; readers can solve alongside him.
encyclopedia-brown-and-the-case-of-the-m.title: Encyclopedia Brown and the Case of the Mysterious Handprints

evy-ivy-over.note: Published by F. Watts in 1978; the sequel is Julie's Daughter. Author appears as Colby F. Rodowsky.
evy-ivy-over.summary: Slug, a girl known as Mary Rose October, lives with her grandmother Gussie, who has the gift of ESP. As Slug grows older she begins to see her grandmother differently.
evy-ivy-over.title: Evy-Ivy-Over

characters: Boggis, Bunce and Bean — greedy, mean farmers
fantastic-mr-fox.summary: Mr. Fox keeps his family fed by raiding three mean farmers. When the farmers set out to dig him out, the animals of the countryside work together.
fantastic-mr-fox.title: Fantastic Mr. Fox

far-out-the-long-canal.note: Plot and characters could not be verified beyond catalog subjects (Netherlands, skating). Illustrator confirmed by Open Library.
far-out-the-long-canal.summary: A Dutch children's novel by Meindert DeJong, set in the Netherlands and centered on skating. Published by Harper & Row in 1964 with illustrations by Nancy Grossman.
far-out-the-long-canal.title: Far Out the Long Canal

father-s-arcane-daughter.note: Year 1976 confirmed (reissued as My Father's Daughter; 1990 TV film Caroline?). The page gives no plot or characters; those are from the original notes and unverified. Setting set to null.
father-s-arcane-daughter.summary: A young woman long believed kidnapped returns to a wealthy family, and her half-brother and half-sister start to wonder if she is who she claims to be. It is a quiet mystery about family and identity.
father-s-arcane-daughter.title: Father's Arcane Daughter

figgs-phantoms.summary: Mona Figg, a girl from a family of eccentric show people, sets out to Capri, a strange afterlife of her own for her loved ones. It is a bittersweet, offbeat tale of family, books and belonging.
figgs-phantoms.title: Figgs & Phantoms

five-children-and-it.summary: Five siblings find a grumpy sand-fairy who grants them one wish a day. Each wish ends up turning out in unexpected ways.
five-children-and-it.title: Five Children and It

free-land.note: Corrected family name (Beaton, not Beach) and the date (1880s). Inspired by Laura Ingalls Wilder's family. Reading age unverified; null.
free-land.summary: Newlyweds, the Beatons, take up a 300-acre homestead on the Dakota prairie and fight cyclones, blizzards and drought to make a living. It was serialized in the Saturday Evening Post before book publication.
free-land.title: Free Land

characters: Mrs. Frankweiler — wealthy, sharp-witted old woman
from-the-mixed-up-files-of-mrs-basil-e-f.summary: Claudia runs away from home with her little brother Jamie and hides in the Metropolitan Museum of Art. They get drawn into the mystery of a statue that may be a Michelangelo.
from-the-mixed-up-files-of-mrs-basil-e-f.title: From the Mixed-Up Files of Mrs. Basil E. Frankweiler

characters: Harriett Weaver — park ranger who adopts him
frosty-a-raccoon-to-remember.note: Draft said 'a family adopts a raccoon'; corrected to a ranger memoir. Open Library gives 1973 (a review elsewhere says 1974). Author's first name appears as Harriet or Harriett.
frosty-a-raccoon-to-remember.summary: A true story by a park ranger who finds an orphaned raccoon and adopts him. Frosty's intelligence and mischief change her life at Big Basin Redwood Park.
frosty-a-raccoon-to-remember.title: Frosty: A Raccoon to Remember

gaffer-samson-s-luck.summary: James is a newcomer to a Fen village who befriends old Gaffer Samson, and they share a story from the past. It deals with courage and friendship.
gaffer-samson-s-luck.title: Gaffer Samson's Luck

characters: His young master — the boy who raises him
Ghond — a hunter who travels with them
gay-neck-the-story-of-a-pigeon.note: Ghond is a hunter, not the young master; setting extended to WWI Europe. Published by E. P. Dutton.
gay-neck-the-story-of-a-pigeon.setting: India, the Himalayas and World War I Europe
gay-neck-the-story-of-a-pigeon.summary: Gay-Neck, a prized pigeon in India, is raised by a boy, is frightened by hawks and is healed at a Buddhist lamasery. He later carries messages in World War I and has to recover from what he sees.
gay-neck-the-story-of-a-pigeon.title: Gay-Neck: The Story of a Pigeon

gentle-ben.summary: Mark, a boy in Alaska, befriends a giant brown bear named Ben kept in a shed. His father worries that Ben is dangerous.
gentle-ben.title: Gentle Ben

george-s-marvelous-medicine.summary: Left alone with his grumpy grandmother, George decides to cook up a new medicine for her from everything in the house. The results are far bigger than he planned.
george-s-marvelous-medicine.title: George's Marvelous Medicine

characters: Purrloom Popcorn — Cornish Rex cat with a ghost-seeing eye
Lydia — his elderly breeder and owner
A young girl — wants a cat
ghost-eye.summary: Purrloom Popcorn is a prize-winning Cornish Rex cat with one blue eye and one gold eye, and the blue eye lets him see ghosts. When his elderly owner Lydia is gone, he is sent to her old house, which is now home to her great-nephew's family. The ghosts he meets turn out to be fairly harmless.
ghost-eye.title: Ghost Eye

ghosts-a-classic-collection.note: Searched the title with Ingram and Sturrock. The only trace is Open Library's illustrated ghost-story collection 'Ghosts' (Unicorn Publishing House, 1989, illustrated by Walt Sturrock, b. 1961), which may be the same book, but no record shows the subtitle or John Ingram as editor. Not confirmed.
ghosts-a-classic-collection.summary: A collection of ghost stories. Its contents could not be confirmed.
ghosts-a-classic-collection.title: Ghosts: A Classic Collection

ginger-pye.summary: Jerry and Rachel Pye buy a puppy named Ginger with their own money and love him fiercely. When he is stolen they set out to find him, while a mysterious man in a yellow hat lurks.
ginger-pye.title: Ginger Pye

characters: The six Evans children — the treasure hunters
go-to-the-room-of-the-eyes.summary: Six Evans children move into an old house in Seattle and find a cryptic message left by earlier young residents thirty years before. It sets them off on a treasure hunt.
go-to-the-room-of-the-eyes.title: Go to the Room of the Eyes

going-solo.setting: East Africa, Greece and the Middle East, 1930s-1940s
going-solo.summary: The second part of Dahl's memoir, covering his years working in East Africa and then as a fighter pilot in World War II. It's full of snakes, close calls and dry humor.
going-solo.title: Going Solo

granny-reardun.summary: Joseph, Mary's son, wants to be a blacksmith like his grandfather, but is drawn to the work of the masons. The story follows his choices about craft and family pride.
granny-reardun.title: Granny Reardun

characters: Pip — humble boy with great hopes
great-expectations.setting: Kent marshes and London, early 19th century
great-expectations.summary: Orphan Pip, raised by his sister and her blacksmith husband, comes into mysterious wealth and moves to London. He learns who his friends truly are.
great-expectations.title: Great Expectations

characters: Will Stanton — seventh son, last Old One
Merriman Lyon — Old One, wise mentor
Bran Davies — pale boy with white hair
Simon Drew — eldest of the Drews
greenwitch.summary: The stolen grail is back in play as the Drews, Will and Merriman return to Cornwall. A mysterious ritual image woven from branches called the Greenwitch holds the secret they need.
greenwitch.title: Greenwitch

gulliver-s-travels.summary: Lemuel Gulliver is shipwrecked among tiny Lilliputians, giant Brobdingnagians and other strange peoples. Swift uses these voyages to poke fun at human nature.
gulliver-s-travels.title: Gulliver's Travels

haji-of-the-elephants.note: Published by McGraw-Hill in 1976. Willis Lindquist also wrote Burma Boy (1953), whose hero is also named Haji and rides elephants; it may be an earlier or related story, not confirmed. Setting inferred from that book.
haji-of-the-elephants.summary: Haji's greatest wish comes true when he is given a mighty elephant to ride. He then faces a dangerous stretch in which both animals and people threaten him.
haji-of-the-elephants.title: Haji of the Elephants

harriet-the-spy.setting: Upper East Side, New York City, 1960s
harriet-the-spy.summary: Harriet M. Welsch, an eleven-year-old New Yorker, spies on neighbors and classmates and records her honest observations in a notebook. When the notebook is found, trouble follows.
harriet-the-spy.title: Harriet the Spy

awards: British Book Awards Children's Book of the Year
harry-potter-and-the-sorcerer-s-stone.note: First published in the UK 1997 as Philosopher's Stone; the US Sorcerer's Stone edition (Scholastic) appeared in 1998.
harry-potter-and-the-sorcerer-s-stone.setting: England: Little Whinging, Hogwarts, Diagon Alley
harry-potter-and-the-sorcerer-s-stone.summary: On his eleventh birthday Harry Potter, raised by unkind relatives, learns he is a wizard and goes to Hogwarts. There he makes friends and gets drawn into a mystery about a guarded magical object and the dark wizard Voldemort.
harry-potter-and-the-sorcerer-s-stone.title: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone

harry-potter-series.note: First UK publication 26 June 1997; Deathly Hallows 21 July 2007.
harry-potter-series.summary: Seven novels follow Harry Potter, a young wizard, through his years at Hogwarts and his conflict with the dark wizard Voldemort. Friendship and courage run through the series.
harry-potter-series.title: Harry Potter series

harry-s-mad.summary: Harry inherits an old parrot who can talk. The bird is unexpectedly wise.
harry-s-mad.title: Harry's Mad

harvey-s-horrible-snake-disaster.note: Series position (#1) inferred from the 1984 start date of the four-book Harvey and Nora series on Eth Clifford's Wikipedia page. Illustrator not found.
harvey-s-horrible-snake-disaster.summary: Ten-year-old Harvey's visit from his cousin Nora leads to trouble involving snakes. It is the first of Eth Clifford's Harvey and Nora books.
harvey-s-horrible-snake-disaster.title: Harvey's Horrible Snake Disaster

heidi.summary: An orphan girl goes to live with her grandfather in the Swiss Alps and brings joy to those around her.
heidi.title: Heidi

characters: Grace Jones — imaginative girl who believes she will be queen
her-majesty-grace-jones.note: US title is The Majesty of Grace (1961); Her Majesty, Grace Jones is an alternate title. Illustrated by Langton herself, not Emily Arnold McCully.
her-majesty-grace-jones.summary: Set during the Depression, this book follows Grace Jones, a girl who imagines she is the eldest daughter of King George VI and so the future Queen of England. It was Langton's first book for children.
her-majesty-grace-jones.title: Her Majesty, Grace Jones

characters: Steps High Like an Elk — their ancestor
high-elk-s-treasure.summary: Thirteen-year-old Joe High Elk searches for a valuable filly lost in a storm. Sheltering in an ancestor's cave with his sister Marie, he makes a discovery of historical importance.
high-elk-s-treasure.title: High Elk's Treasure

hitty-her-first-hundred-years.summary: Hitty is a small wooden doll who narrates her hundred years of travels from Maine to the South Seas and India. She sees history through a doll's eyes.
hitty-her-first-hundred-years.title: Hitty, Her First Hundred Years

homer-price.summary: Homer Price lives in the small town of Centerburg and is involved in zany adventures with a runaway doughnut machine, bandits and a mouse-free lunch counter.
homer-price.title: Homer Price

homesick-my-own-story.summary: Jean Fritz remembers her childhood in China in the 1920s, longing for a home she had never seen in America. A warm memoir.
homesick-my-own-story.title: Homesick: My Own Story

humbug-mountain.summary: A newspaper man and his family move to the Western town of Humbug Mountain. They end up in a gold-strike mystery and a ghost-town scheme.
humbug-mountain.title: Humbug Mountain

hurry-home-candy.setting: A city and countryside in mid-20th century America
hurry-home-candy.summary: A small dog named Candy is swept away from his family and has to survive on the streets and in strange homes. The story follows his long hope of making his way back.
hurry-home-candy.title: Hurry Home, Candy

hyenas.note: Published by Dodd, Mead. Hopf also published as A. M. Lightner for science fiction.
hyenas.summary: An introduction to the hyena, a misunderstood animal related to civets and mongooses and widely hated in Africa. The book describes how it lives and why its reputation is unfair.
hyenas.title: Hyenas

i-juan-de-pareja.summary: Told by Juan de Pareja, an enslaved assistant to the painter Diego Velázquez, who learns to paint in secret. It follows his journey toward freedom and a place in art.
i-juan-de-pareja.title: I, Juan de Pareja

characters: Atu — the polar bear, the Ice King
ice-king.note: Earlier draft guessed historical fiction/biography and could not identify it; Open Library and library catalogs list Ice King (Scribner, 1965) by Ernestine N. Byrd as polar bear fiction. Illustrator Marilyn Miller from a catalog description found by search.
ice-king.summary: A children's novel about a polar bear named Atu, called the Ice King, following his life from cubhood through the loss of his parents and encounters with the Smith Sound Eskimos of northern Greenland.
ice-king.title: Ice King

in-bikole-eight-modern-stories-of-life-i.note: Open Library lists In Bikole by Tom Gilroy, first published 1978 (publisher not shown); a library catalog confirms the title and subtitle. Draft story details (folk tales, reading age) not confirmed.
in-bikole-eight-modern-stories-of-life-i.summary: A collection of eight modern stories about life in a West African village. Little else about its contents could be verified.
in-bikole-eight-modern-stories-of-life-i.title: In Bikole: Eight Modern Stories of Life in a West African Village

in-dubious-battle.summary: Organizers try to lead migrant apple pickers in a strike in a California valley during the Depression. The novel looks hard at idealism, loyalty and the cost of a cause.
in-dubious-battle.title: In Dubious Battle

in-face-of-danger.note: Previously marked unidentified. Open Library lists In face of danger by Mara Kay, first published 1977, subject Fiction; Jews. Genre and setting are not verified.
in-face-of-danger.summary: A 1977 novel for young readers by Mara Kay, catalogued under fiction about Jews. No plot description was found, so the story is not summarized.
in-face-of-danger.title: In Face of Danger

in-search-of-tutankhamun.note: Open Library lists the 1985 edition under Ventura and a 1987 omnibus (with Crete and Troy) under Ventura and Ceserani, so Ceserani's role is only partly confirmed. Wikipedia source was wrong; replaced.
in-search-of-tutankhamun.summary: An illustrated account of the search for and discovery of Tutankhamun's tomb. Large pictures and short text show how archaeologists worked in Egypt.
in-search-of-tutankhamun.title: In Search of Tutankhamun

in-the-beginning-creation-stories-from-a.summary: Twenty-five creation myths from cultures around the world are retold in lyrical prose.
in-the-beginning-creation-stories-from-a.title: In the Beginning: Creation Stories from Around the World

in-the-days-of-giants-a-book-of-norse-ta.summary: A retelling of Norse myths for children, with Odin, Thor and Loki. The tales cover gods, giants and tricks.
in-the-days-of-giants-a-book-of-norse-ta.title: In the Days of Giants: A Book of Norse Tales

incognito-mosquito-private-insective.note: First published 1982 (Lothrop, Lee and Shepard); sequels followed in 1986 and 1987. Author's full name not found.
incognito-mosquito-private-insective.summary: A mosquito detective recounts his cases and run-ins with other insect characters to a young reporter, in a send-up of private-eye stories.
incognito-mosquito-private-insective.title: Incognito Mosquito, Private Insective

indian-sleep-man-tales.note: Caxton Printers, Caldwell, Idaho; first dated 1940 (Open Library), with a 1947 printing. Illustrator credit comes from a bookseller listing.
indian-sleep-man-tales.setting: Otoe reservation near Red Rock, Oklahoma
indian-sleep-man-tales.summary: A collection of Otoe bedtime tales gathered by Bernice G. Anderson on visits to the Otoe reservation in Oklahoma. The stories explain features of nature such as the rabbit's pink eyes and the man in the moon.
indian-sleep-man-tales.title: Indian Sleep-Man Tales

island-of-the-blue-dolphins.summary: Karana is left alone on a Pacific island after her tribe leaves. She builds shelter, hunts, and befriends animals for years.
island-of-the-blue-dolphins.title: Island of the Blue Dolphins

characters: Jill (Janey Pecq) — high-spirited girl from a poorer family
jack-and-jill.note: Subtitle article is the correct page. Names and setting added.
jack-and-jill.summary: After a sledding crash, neighbors Jack and Jill are laid up for months in a New England village. With their families and friends they learn patience and kindness, and take on small projects to improve their lives. It first ran in St. Nicholas magazine.
jack-and-jill.title: Jack and Jill

jacob-have-i-loved.summary: Louise grows up on a Chesapeake Bay island feeling overshadowed by her talented twin sister. She slowly finds her own path.
jacob-have-i-loved.title: Jacob Have I Loved

characters: Aunt Sponge and Aunt Spiker — cruel, selfish aunts
james-and-the-giant-peach.setting: Southern England and the Atlantic Ocean, mid-20th century
james-and-the-giant-peach.summary: Orphaned James lives with two dreadful aunts until a magic accident grows an enormous peach. Inside it he befriends giant talking insects, and together they float off across the ocean.
james-and-the-giant-peach.title: James and the Giant Peach

characters: Mr. Rochester — brooding master of Thornfield
jane-eyre.summary: Orphaned Jane is mistreated in her aunt's house and at school, then becomes a governess at Thornfield Hall, where she meets the brooding Mr. Rochester and a strange secret. A story of independence and moral courage.
jane-eyre.title: Jane Eyre

jennifer-hecate-macbeth-william-mckinley.setting: A small town in New York State, 1960s
jennifer-hecate-macbeth-william-mckinley.summary: Lonely new girl Elizabeth befriends Jennifer, who claims to be a witch. Elizabeth becomes her apprentice, with odd tasks and eventually a test of their friendship.
jennifer-hecate-macbeth-william-mckinley.title: Jennifer, Hecate, Macbeth, William McKinley, and Me, Elizabeth

jimmy-the-pickpocket-of-the-palace.series: Sequel to The Prince of the Pond (1992)
jimmy-the-pickpocket-of-the-palace.setting: A pond and a royal palace
jimmy-the-pickpocket-of-the-palace.summary: Jimmy is the frog-son of the frog prince, and he must stop a hag from draining his pond. He is turned into a human boy and put to work in the palace, where a spirited princess helps and hinders him.
jimmy-the-pickpocket-of-the-palace.title: Jimmy, the Pickpocket of the Palace

johnny-tremain.summary: A silversmith's apprentice in Boston meets leaders of the American Revolution.
johnny-tremain.title: Johnny Tremain

awards: National Book Award for Young People's Literature 1969 (first winner)
characters: Grandfather — his companion on the journey
journey-from-peppermint-street.note: Draft character names unverified; only Siebren and his grandfather and the aunt are confirmed.
journey-from-peppermint-street.summary: In a Dutch coastal village in the early 1900s, young Siebren travels at night with his grandfather to visit a sick aunt. The journey is full of odd encounters and small discoveries.
journey-from-peppermint-street.title: Journey from Peppermint Street

journey-to-america.summary: In 1938, a Jewish family flees Nazi Germany. The father goes ahead to America, and the mother and daughters try to follow.
journey-to-america.title: Journey to America

characters: Amaroq — leader of the wolf pack
julie-of-the-wolves.summary: Thirteen-year-old Miyax runs away across the Alaskan tundra and must survive. A pack of wolves comes to accept her.
julie-of-the-wolves.title: Julie of the Wolves

jurassic-park.note: Adult novel; not a children's read-aloud. Published October 1990 by Knopf.
jurassic-park.summary: Scientists and investors tour a theme park on a Costa Rican island where dinosaurs have been cloned. When the park's security is sabotaged, the animals get loose and the visitors face serious danger.
jurassic-park.title: Jurassic Park

characters: Mahbub Ali — horse trader and spy
kim.summary: Kim, an orphaned Irish boy in British India, becomes the disciple of a Tibetan lama and a spy in the Great Game. A rich adventure full of Indian life.
kim.title: Kim

king-of-the-wind.setting: Morocco, France and England, early 18th century
king-of-the-wind.summary: A mute stable boy named Agba journeys with a golden Arabian horse called Sham from Morocco to France and England. The horse becomes ancestor of the great Thoroughbreds.
king-of-the-wind.title: King of the Wind

knee-knock-rise.summary: Egan visits his aunt and hears of the Megrimum, a fearsome creature said to live on Knee-Knock Rise. He sets out to explore.
knee-knock-rise.title: Knee-Knock Rise

characters: Joe — the narrator and book's owner
knights-of-the-kitchen-table-the-time-wa.note: published_last 2006 = end of the series. Open Library shows a 1987 date, but Wikipedia gives 1991 for the series start; kept 1991. Dragon/giant details from original notes could not be verified and were dropped.
knights-of-the-kitchen-table-the-time-wa.setting: Medieval Camelot, reached from a modern home
knights-of-the-kitchen-table-the-time-wa.summary: Joe, Sam and Fred are pulled into the past by a magic book and land at King Arthur's court. They have to survive the Middle Ages and find a way home. It starts the Time Warp Trio series.
knights-of-the-kitchen-table-the-time-wa.title: Knights of the Kitchen Table (The Time Warp Trio)

lad-a-dog.note: Lad: A Dog redirects to another-language wiki; used the Terhune article. Later Lad books: 1922, 1929 (so published_last 1929). Estate named Sunnybank; 'The Place' naming not confirmed.
lad-a-dog.setting: Sunnybank, Terhune's estate in northern New Jersey, early 1900s
lad-a-dog.summary: A dozen linked stories about a noble collie based on Terhune's own dog. Lad shows loyalty, courage and cleverness as he guards his family's country home.
lad-a-dog.title: Lad: A Dog

lafcadio-the-lion-who-shot-back.note: 'The Hunter — his teacher' replaced by Finchfinger. First appeared in Playboy, Nov 1963.
lafcadio-the-lion-who-shot-back.setting: An African jungle, then a city
lafcadio-the-lion-who-shot-back.summary: Lafcadio, a young lion, learns to shoot a hunter's rifle and is taken to the city, where he becomes a famous circus star and starts acting like a human. Narrated by Silverstein as 'Uncle Shelby', it asks what fame costs.
lafcadio-the-lion-who-shot-back.title: Lafcadio, the Lion Who Shot Back

lake-wobegon-days.summary: Humorous recollections of a fictional small Minnesota town.
lake-wobegon-days.title: Lake Wobegon Days

let-s-investigate-numbers.summary: Hands-on puzzles and activities introduce number ideas to children.
let-s-investigate-numbers.title: Let's Investigate Numbers

lily-and-the-lost-boy.summary: Lily, an American girl living on a Greek island, meets a mysterious American boy. Their friendship helps her see things she had missed.
lily-and-the-lost-boy.title: Lily and the Lost Boy

little-britches.note: Setting dates narrowed to 1906-1910. Published by W. W. Norton, 14 Aug 1950. published_last 1968 = Horse of a Different Color, per the Moody article.
little-britches.summary: A memoir of Ralph Moody's boyhood, when his family moves from New Hampshire to a Colorado ranch because of his father's health. Ralph learns to work like a cowboy and takes on more responsibility.
little-britches.title: Little Britches

characters: Laura Ingalls — the narrator, growing from child to young woman
Ma and Pa Ingalls — her parents
little-house-books.note: Series line. First book Little House in the Big Woods (1932); the last of the core nine, The First Four Years, appeared posthumously in 1971. On the Way Home (1962) and West from Home (1974) are extra books.
little-house-books.setting: Wisconsin, Kansas, Minnesota and Dakota Territory, 1870s-1880s
little-house-books.summary: A series of semi-autobiographical novels following Laura Ingalls and her family as they move across the American frontier in the late 1800s. The books move from the big woods of Wisconsin through prairies, towns and hard winters to Laura's marriage.
little-house-books.title: Little House Books

characters: Laura Ingalls — the author as a girl
little-house-books-complete-set.note: Eight original books 1932-1943; the ninth, The First Four Years, appeared in 1971 and is included in many complete sets. Garth Williams illustrated the uniform edition reissued in 1953, not the originals.
little-house-books-complete-set.summary: Laura Ingalls Wilder's autobiographical series follows a pioneer family from a log cabin in Wisconsin's Big Woods through Kansas, Minnesota and Dakota Territory. The books cover her childhood, her teaching years and her marriage.
little-house-books-complete-set.title: Little House Books (complete set)

characters: Caroline Quiner — five-year-old girl who grows up to be Ma Ingalls
little-house-in-brookfield-little-town-a.note: The notebook line names two books; Little Town at the Crossroads is the second (1997, Open Library). Title expanded to name both. Reading age is the grade 4-7 range given in one listing.
little-house-in-brookfield-little-town-a.summary: Set in 1845, these two books follow young Caroline Quiner, later Laura Ingalls Wilder's mother, in Brookfield, Wisconsin. Her father has been lost at sea, and her family gets through its hardest year with courage and love.
little-house-in-brookfield-little-town-a.title: Little House in Brookfield and Little Town at the Crossroads

characters: The Earl of Dorincourt — stern grandfather
little-lord-fauntleroy.summary: A kind American boy named Cedric discovers he is heir to an English earldom. His good nature softens his gruff grandfather.
little-lord-fauntleroy.title: Little Lord Fauntleroy

little-women.summary: The four March sisters grow up in New England during the Civil War while their father is away. Each has her own dreams, talents and struggles.
little-women.title: Little Women

lizzie-silver-of-sherwood-forest.summary: Lizzie is obsessed with Robin Hood and acts out his sword fights, to her sister Rona's annoyance. Her new obsession follows an earlier one for her pet tarantula.
lizzie-silver-of-sherwood-forest.title: Lizzie Silver of Sherwood Forest

long-claws-an-arctic-adventure.note: A 32-page illustrated book (McClelland & Stewart / Atheneum, 1981), not a long novel. Catalog records misdate the author as 1793-1841. Plot taken from a catalog description.

mary-poppins.summary: The magical, stern Mary Poppins arrives on the East Wind to be nanny to the Banks children and takes them on extraordinary outings. She flatly denies it all.

moon-eyes.setting: A decaying family house in England

moon-flash.summary: A girl in a peaceful forest world sets out to explore the outside after a mysterious event.
moon-flash.title: Moon-Flash

morning-girl.title: Morning Girl

mr-revere-and-i.note: Horse's name corrected from 'Scrawny Sherman' to Scheherazade/Sherry (from a catalog and review via search; the Wikipedia article lacks it). Book article does not exist at the original URL.

mr-revere-and-i.title: Mr. Revere and I

my-side-of-the-mountain.summary: Sam Gribley runs away from his crowded New York apartment to live in the Catskills. He learns to find food, make shelter and train a peregrine falcon.
my-side-of-the-mountain.title: My Side of the Mountain

characters: Althea — her great-grandmother, who grew up in China
mystery-of-the-angry-idol.note: Year confirmed as 1965 (Open Library). Plot details come from reader blurbs found in search results and were not checked against a full synopsis.

mystery-of-the-angry-idol.title: Mystery of the Angry Idol

national-velvet.summary: Velvet Brown wins a horse in a raffle and trains him with the help of a young drifter to run in the Grand National. A beloved tale of devotion between a girl and her horse.

night-birds-on-nantucket.title: Nightbirds on Nantucket

nightbirds-on-nantucket.summary: Dido Twite wakes aboard a whaling ship and ends up on Nantucket looking after the captain's anxious daughter. She uncovers a plot involving a giant cannon aimed at England.
nightbirds-on-nantucket.title: Nightbirds on Nantucket

ninny-s-boat.setting: Denmark and Britain, fifth century AD
ninny-s-boat.summary: Ninny is a slave of the Angles, a tribe planning to sail in search of a new land. His resourcefulness and friendship with the leader Offa win him a place in the boat, and in Britain he discovers he is himself a Briton.
ninny-s-boat.title: Ninny's Boat

characters: Sandy — newcomer from New York City

nobody-likes-trina.title: Nobody Likes Trina

ocelot.note: Goodreads lists Ocelot by B. F. Beebe (with illustrator James Ralph Johnson), but no year or description was found.

of-mice-and-men.title: Of Mice and Men

run-light-buck-run.note: Existence, author, 1962 date and publisher (D. McKay Co.) confirmed by Open Library; plot, genre and characters unverified.

the-cricket-in-times-square.title: The Cricket in Times Square

characters: Dido Twite — sharp-tongued, plucky street girl
the-cuckoo-tree.summary: Dido Twite returns to England and is swept into a plot involving a mysterious chest, a hidden royal threat and a secret society. Packed with chases, villains and cliffhangers.
the-cuckoo-tree.title: The Cuckoo Tree

characters: Walter — boy who helps stranded aliens
the-dandelion-caper.note: Published 1986 by Putnam; the earlier 'puzzling affair involving dandelions' draft was wrong.
the-dandelion-caper.summary: Walter and his friend Kathy have helped many stranded space tourists, and now they face evil aliens in an abandoned house. A cat with unusual powers comes to their aid.
the-dandelion-caper.title: The Dandelion Caper

the-dark-is-rising.note: Added illustrator; Rider/Merriman details unverified beyond series knowledge, so Rider removed.
the-dark-is-rising.setting: Thames Valley, England, from the winter solstice to Twelfth Night
the-dark-is-rising.summary: On his eleventh birthday at midwinter, Will Stanton discovers he is one of the Old Ones, who serve the Light against the Dark. He must gather the Signs to help the Light as magic stirs through the Christmas season.
the-dark-is-rising.title: The Dark Is Rising

the-dark-thirty-southern-tales-of-the-su.summary: Ghost stories drawn from African American tradition, each reflecting history and community. Told at dusk, they are spooky and thought-provoking.
the-dark-thirty-southern-tales-of-the-su.title: The Dark-Thirty: Southern Tales of the Supernatural

the-devil-s-other-storybook.note: Collection has ten stories; age 8-12 per Publishers Weekly (search snippet).
the-devil-s-other-storybook.summary: Ten more tales about the Devil, mostly set in the afterlife, where a lazy Satan dispenses poetic rather than gruesome justice. Witty and good for reading aloud.
the-devil-s-other-storybook.title: The Devil's Other Storybook

the-digging-badger.summary: A children's nonfiction book on the body, habits and habitat of the North American badger and its relatives.
the-digging-badger.title: The Digging Badger

the-door-in-the-hedge.summary: A collection of four fairy tales, including two retold classics. Princesses, enchantments and difficult choices run through each.
the-door-in-the-hedge.title: The Door in the Hedge

the-door-in-the-wall.summary: Robin, a boy in medieval England, loses the use of his legs and must find new ways to serve his king.
the-door-in-the-wall.title: The Door in the Wall

characters: The lady of the manor — dragon's friend
the-dragon-of-og.summary: Based on a Scottish Lowlands legend, a luck-bringing dragon has long received two bullocks a month. When Angus Og inherits the castle he insists the dragon must die, and a contest of wits begins.
the-dragon-of-og.title: The Dragon of Og

the-dragon-that-lived-under-manhattan.note: Published by Crown, Oct 1970. Kirkus review is unenthusiastic about the second half.
the-dragon-that-lived-under-manhattan.summary: A boy named Jimmy meets a prince who has come to New York to hunt a dragon hiding in the subway tunnels. The dragon later strikes a deal with the city's officials.
the-dragon-that-lived-under-manhattan.title: The Dragon That Lived Under Manhattan

the-dragons-of-blueland.summary: Elmer Elevator, a boy, and his dragon Boris return to save dragons.
the-dragons-of-blueland.title: The Dragons of Blueland

characters: Twig — young hero of the Twig Saga
the-edge-chronicles.note: Parts: Beyond the Deepwoods 1998, Stormchaser 1999, Midnight Over Sanctaphrax 2000. Other draft character names were not confirmed.
the-edge-chronicles.setting: The Edge, a vast cliff world
the-edge-chronicles.summary: Twig, the hero of the Twig Saga, journeys through the strange lands of the Edge, a vast cliff with no apparent bottom. The first three books in the notebook line are Beyond the Deepwoods, Stormchaser and Midnight Over Sanctaphrax.
the-edge-chronicles.title: The Edge Chronicles

the-egypt-game.summary: Children in an apartment neighborhood build a secret world of ancient Egypt in a deserted yard. Their play is interrupted by a real danger in the neighborhood.
the-egypt-game.title: The Egypt Game

the-enchanted-raisin.identified: Previously unidentified. English edition 1988 (Latin American Literary Review Press, per Open Library and Publishers Weekly); Goodreads and a French listing seen in search suggest the stories first appeared around 1984. Original Spanish title not verified.
the-enchanted-raisin.summary: A collection of Chilean children's fairy tales in English translation. In the title story, three incorrigible boys wear their mother out until she shrivels into a raisin. Other stories include 'The Buried Giant' and 'The Princess and the Green Dwarf'.
the-enchanted-raisin.title: The Enchanted Raisin

the-enchanter-s-spell-five-famous-tales.summary: Spirin retells and illustrates five famous tales: Little Daylight, The Princess and the Seven Brothers, The Nutcracker, The Beautiful Kitchen Maid and The Emperor's New Clothes. Each gets its own period setting in his paintings.
the-enchanter-s-spell-five-famous-tales.title: The Enchanter's Spell: Five Famous Tales

characters: Nate Twitchell — practical New Hampshire boy
the-enormous-egg.summary: A boy named Nate Twitchell's hen lays an enormous egg that hatches into a baby triceratops. Nate raises it and the family becomes famous.
the-enormous-egg.title: The Enormous Egg

characters: Moominpappa — the author of the memoirs
The Joxter and the Muddler — fellow adventurers
the-exploits-of-moominpappa.note: Jansson revised it in 1968 as Moominpappa's Memoirs; sources differ on the English release date.
the-exploits-of-moominpappa.setting: Finland-inspired Moominvalley and the seas beyond
the-exploits-of-moominpappa.summary: Moominpappa writes his memoirs for Moomintroll, Sniff and Snufkin. He tells of running away from a foundling home and sailing off with Hodgkins and other friends in a boat.
the-exploits-of-moominpappa.title: The Exploits of Moominpappa

the-falcon-bow-an-arctic-legend.note: Published by McClelland and Stewart. Plot details come from a search snippet (publisher page not fetched).
the-falcon-bow-an-arctic-legend.setting: The Keewatin region of the Arctic
the-falcon-bow-an-arctic-legend.summary: Kungo, an Inuk, travels into Indian country when the caribou fail to return and fires are blamed on neighbors. He and his sister Shulu work for peace between the two peoples.
the-falcon-bow-an-arctic-legend.title: The Falcon Bow: An Arctic Legend

characters: David Stanley — tries to befriend the kidnappers
Amanda Stanley — her bragging about her rich father leads to the kidnapping
the-famous-stanley-kidnapping-case.note: Atheneum, 1979. Draft illustrator Alton Raible could not be confirmed and is removed. Plot from a catalog description and a search result.
the-famous-stanley-kidnapping-case.summary: The Stanley family is living in Italy when the children are kidnapped. The captive children give their incompetent kidnappers advice on running a better kidnapping and on nutrition.
the-famous-stanley-kidnapping-case.title: The Famous Stanley Kidnapping Case

characters: Lukas-Kasha — lazy young man turned king
Nur-Jehan — enslaved girl in the palace
the-first-two-lives-of-lukas-kasha.note: E.P. Dutton, 1978. Draft character 'Nur-Jan' corrected to Nur-Jehan and 'shy' corrected to 'lazy'.
the-first-two-lives-of-lukas-kasha.setting: Zara-Petra and the kingdom of Abadan (royal city Shirazan)
the-first-two-lives-of-lukas-kasha.summary: Lukas-Kasha, a lazy young man, joins a magic show and is carried to the city of Abadan, where he is proclaimed king. He finds that ruling takes more than comfort and runs into powerful opposition when he tries to change things.
the-first-two-lives-of-lukas-kasha.title: The First Two Lives of Lukas-Kasha

the-fledgling.note: Corrected heroine surname to Dorian and goose to Goose Prince; illustrator unverified so null.
the-fledgling.summary: Georgie Dorian believes she can fly and is taught by a Canada goose called the Goose Prince. A hunter obsessed with the bird threatens them in Concord.
the-fledgling.title: The Fledgling

the-foxman.summary: A teenager is sent to live in the wilderness with a mysterious man with a scarred face. Their bond grows.
the-foxman.title: The Foxman

the-garden-under-the-sea.note: Viking, 1957. The draft's illustrator Garth Williams is not supported: a catalog snippet seen in search credits Garry MacKenzie, but this was not confirmed, so left blank. Also issued as Oscar Lobster's Fair Exchange (1966).
the-garden-under-the-sea.setting: Long Island Sound, near Turtle Rock
the-garden-under-the-sea.summary: Sea creatures off Long Island Sound are angry at humans who carry shells and other treasures away from the shore. They build a garden of their own out of human relics. The gentle episodic tale carries a message about taking only what you need.
the-garden-under-the-sea.title: The Garden Under the Sea

the-giant.note: Identified as the Viking Press 1954 book; the vague earlier summary was replaced.
the-giant.summary: An eight-year-old boy is seven stories tall because he has a perfect digestive system. His family and friends try to hide him, so the narrator befriends him and plans a way for him to live openly.
the-giant.title: The Giant

characters: Katie Welker — girl with silver eyes and telekinesis
the-girl-with-the-silver-eyes.summary: Katie Welker has silver eyes and can move things by thinking about them. People fear her, so she wonders whether other children like her exist.
the-girl-with-the-silver-eyes.title: The Girl with the Silver Eyes

characters: The Giver — old keeper of memories
the-giver.summary: Jonas lives in a seemingly perfect community where everything is controlled. When he is chosen to receive its memories, he starts to question everything.
the-giver.title: The Giver

the-good-earth.summary: Wang Lung, a poor Chinese farmer, works and rises through hardship.
the-good-earth.title: The Good Earth

the-good-master.summary: Wild city girl Kate is sent to live on her uncle's Hungarian ranch, where she and her cousin Jancsi grow up together amid horses, festivals and the coming of war.
the-good-master.title: The Good Master

the-great-brain.summary: Narrated by J.D., this tells of his clever older brother Tom, who uses his wits to make money and fix problems in a small Utah town. Many of his schemes help others, and many pay Tom.
the-great-brain.title: The Great Brain

the-great-brain-at-the-academy.summary: Tom is sent off to a Catholic boarding school in Salt Lake City, where his schemes meet stiffer opposition. Back home J.D. misses him despite himself.
the-great-brain-at-the-academy.title: The Great Brain at the Academy

the-great-brain-reforms.summary: Tom returns home and tries to turn over a new leaf, while still using his brains on town troubles. J.D. watches the results.
the-great-brain-reforms.title: The Great Brain Reforms

characters: Gilly Hopkins — prickly, clever foster child
the-great-gilly-hopkins.summary: Eleven-year-old Gilly, a tough foster child, arrives at a new home and schemes to find her birth mother. She slowly learns what family can be.
the-great-gilly-hopkins.title: The Great Gilly Hopkins

the-green-book.note: First published London 1981 (Macmillan); US edition 1982 illustrated by Lloyd Bloom; reissued as Shine (1988). Plot details from search snippets.
the-green-book.summary: As Earth dies, a group of refugees including a girl named Pattie flee in an old spaceship to a new planet. The colony struggles to survive there.
the-green-book.title: The Green Book

characters: Will Stanton — seventh son, last Old One
Bran Davies — pale boy with white hair
Merriman Lyon — Old One, wise mentor
the-grey-king.summary: Will, recovering from illness, goes to Wales to find the golden harp that will wake the sleeping Sleepers. There he befriends an odd, white-haired boy and fights an ancient evil in the hills.
the-grey-king.title: The Grey King

the-happiest-ending.summary: Twelve-year-old Rinko learns about love, family and an arranged marriage in a Japanese-American community in California.
the-happiest-ending.title: The Happiest Ending

the-haunting.summary: Barney is haunted by a ghostly figure who seems to be his late relative. His family's secrets slowly emerge, and he must survive the mystery.
the-haunting.title: The Haunting

the-headless-cupid.summary: David's new stepfamily moves into a big house where a poltergeist seems to be at work. His stepsister Amanda plots to explore the occult.
the-headless-cupid.title: The Headless Cupid

the-hero-and-the-crown.summary: Aerin, the king's daughter, is an outcast in her own court. She learns to fight dragons and takes up a quest to protect the kingdom.
the-hero-and-the-crown.title: The Hero and the Crown

the-high-king.note: Doli removed from main characters; summary rewritten to remove Dyrnwyn-delivery detail.
the-high-king.summary: War engulfs Prydain as Arawn's forces strike, and Taran and his companions rally the land against him. It concludes the Chronicles of Prydain.
the-high-king.title: The High King

awards: New York Herald Tribune Children's Spring Book Festival prize 1938
characters: Gollum — riddling creature of the dark
the-hobbit.summary: Bilbo Baggins, a comfortable hobbit, is whisked away by a wizard and thirteen dwarves to win back treasure from a dragon. He discovers unexpected courage and cleverness along the way.
the-hobbit.title: The Hobbit

the-horse-and-his-boy.setting: Calormen, Archenland and Narnia, during the Pevensies' reign
the-horse-and-his-boy.summary: A boy named Shasta and a talking horse, Bree, flee the southern land of Calormen toward Narnia. On the way they meet a proud girl, Aravis, and learn of a danger threatening the north.
the-horse-and-his-boy.title: The Horse and His Boy

the-house-at-pooh-corner.summary: Winnie-the-Pooh and friends have more adventures in the Hundred Acre Wood, including meeting Tigger. The book includes the famous Poohsticks game.
the-house-at-pooh-corner.title: The House at Pooh Corner

the-house-on-the-hill.summary: Twelve-year-old Philip is sent to stay with his great-aunt and cousin in a decaying Glasgow mansion. The cousins notice a light in a long-empty room and photos showing furniture that is not there.
the-house-on-the-hill.title: The House on the Hill

the-hundred-and-one-dalmatians.summary: Pongo and Missis rescue their puppies and dozens of others from the wicked Cruella de Vil.
the-hundred-and-one-dalmatians.title: The Hundred and One Dalmatians

the-hundred-dresses.summary: Wanda Petronski, a poor Polish girl, says she owns a hundred dresses at home, and classmates tease her. The story gently examines cruelty, silence and regret.
the-hundred-dresses.title: The Hundred Dresses

characters: Kwan — her older sister who sees ghosts
the-hundred-secret-senses.summary: Olivia, a Chinese-American photographer, is embarrassed by her half-sister Kwan, who claims to see ghosts and remembers past lives. Kwan arranges a trip to China that is really a scheme to reconcile Olivia with her estranged husband.
the-hundred-secret-senses.title: The Hundred Secret Senses

the-iceberg-hermit.note: Author appears in catalogs as Arthur J. Roth. Year 1974 from Open Library (Four Winds Press/Scholastic). The draft's unverified Newbery claim was removed.
the-iceberg-hermit.summary: Shipwrecked in 1757, seventeen-year-old Allan is stranded on an iceberg in the Arctic seas with only an orphaned polar bear cub for company. He begins a struggle to survive.
the-iceberg-hermit.title: The Iceberg Hermit

the-incredible-journey.summary: A Labrador, a bull terrier and a Siamese cat set out across Canadian wilderness to find their family. The three animals help each other along the way.
the-incredible-journey.title: The Incredible Journey

the-indian-in-the-cupboard.summary: Omri's birthday cupboard turns plastic toys into living people. His tiny new friend challenges Omri to think about responsibility.
the-indian-in-the-cupboard.title: The Indian in the Cupboard

characters: Tamar — king bound by his word
the-iron-ring.setting: A mythical India of humans and talking animals
the-iron-ring.summary: King Tamar of Sundari loses a dice game to the maharajah Jaya and is bound by an iron ring, so honor sends him on a long journey. Along the way he gathers odd companions, including a monkey king, a cowgirl and a gloomy eagle. The adventure is set in a land inspired by Indian mythology.
the-iron-ring.title: The Iron Ring

the-island-on-bird-street.note: Hebrew original 1981 (Keter); English translation by Hillel Halkin, 1984.
the-island-on-bird-street.setting: A ghetto in occupied Poland, World War II
the-island-on-bird-street.summary: Eleven-year-old Alex, a Jewish boy in a ghetto in occupied Poland, is separated from his father when deportations begin. Alone in a bombed-out building, he must find food and avoid soldiers while he waits for his father to return.
the-island-on-bird-street.title: The Island on Bird Street

the-joke-shop.note: First in Enright's Atlantis series (Chatto and Windus, London), per SF Encyclopedia; sequels 1978 and 1979.
the-joke-shop.setting: A fantasy world beyond an invisible border
the-joke-shop.summary: Three children cross an invisible border into a frightening world, where they are captured. Later they question whether they want to be rescued.
the-joke-shop.title: The Joke Shop

the-jungle.summary: A Lithuanian immigrant family comes to Chicago hoping for a better life and meets brutal work and poverty in the meatpacking plants. The book exposed unsanitary conditions in the industry.
the-jungle.title: The Jungle

the-king-s-fifth.summary: A young mapmaker joins a Spanish expedition seeking the golden cities of Cibola, and is later put on trial in Spain. The tale shows gold greed and its price.
the-king-s-fifth.title: The King's Fifth

the-last-battle.summary: A false Aslan appears in Narnia's last days and King Tirian struggles to expose the deceit. The story brings the series to its close.
the-last-battle.title: The Last Battle

the-last-slice-of-rainbow.note: Open Library confirms title, 1985 date and illustrator Alix Berenzy; individual stories not verified.
the-last-slice-of-rainbow.summary: A collection of fairy-tale style fantasy stories by Joan Aiken. Published in 1985 by Jonathan Cape and Harper & Row.
the-last-slice-of-rainbow.title: The Last Slice of Rainbow and Other Stories

characters: Lucy Pevensie — first to find Narnia
the-lion-the-witch-and-the-wardrobe.setting: Narnia and an English country house, WWII
the-lion-the-witch-and-the-wardrobe.summary: Four evacuated siblings find a wardrobe leading to Narnia, locked in endless winter under the White Witch. With help from the lion Aslan they work to end her rule.
the-lion-the-witch-and-the-wardrobe.title: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe

the-little-bookroom.summary: A collection of Farjeon's own favourite short stories and fairy tales, with a mix of fantasy and gentle humor.
the-little-bookroom.title: The Little Bookroom

the-little-cow-and-the-turtle.note: Harper & Brothers, 1955, 178 pp.; Sendak illustrated. Draft setting not confirmed.
the-little-cow-and-the-turtle.summary: A little cow grows bored with pasture life and goes in search of adventure. She befriends a slow old mud turtle, among others.
the-little-cow-and-the-turtle.title: The Little Cow and the Turtle

characters: The little mermaid — youngest sea princess
The sea witch — dealer in dangerous bargains
the-little-mermaid.setting: The sea and a seaside kingdom, long ago
the-little-mermaid.summary: A young mermaid longs for a human soul and falls in love with a prince, trading her voice for a chance to walk on land. A bittersweet fairy tale about love and sacrifice.
the-little-mermaid.title: The Little Mermaid

the-long-journey.note: Atheneum, 1970 per Open Library search; Aladdin paperback 1974. Details are from a one-line catalog summary.
the-long-journey.summary: A young girl rides alone across Montana to get help for her grandfather, who is going blind.
the-long-journey.title: The Long Journey

the-lord-of-the-rings.summary: Frodo Baggins and his companions set out to destroy a ring forged by the Dark Lord Sauron by casting it into Mount Doom. The story was published in three volumes: The Fellowship of the Ring, The Two Towers and The Return of the King.
the-lord-of-the-rings.title: The Lord of the Rings

the-lord-of-the-rings-trilogy-and-the-ho.note: The Hobbit 1937; The Lord of the Rings published in three volumes 1954-1955.
the-lord-of-the-rings-trilogy-and-the-ho.summary: Bilbo Baggins joins a company of dwarves to win back a treasure from a dragon in The Hobbit. The Lord of the Rings follows the quest to destroy a ruling ring of power.
the-lord-of-the-rings-trilogy-and-the-ho.title: The Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit (4-book set)

the-lord-of-the-rings-trilogy-the-fellow.note: Fellowship July 1954, Two Towers Nov 1954, Return of the King Oct 1955.
the-lord-of-the-rings-trilogy-the-fellow.series: The Lord of the Rings (3 volumes)
the-lord-of-the-rings-trilogy-the-fellow.summary: The hobbit Frodo sets out from the Shire to deal with a ring of great power, pursued by enemies and joined by companions. Together they resist the Dark Lord Sauron.
the-lord-of-the-rings-trilogy-the-fellow.title: The Lord of the Rings Trilogy

the-magic-hat-of-mortimer-wintergreen.note: Open Library confirms 1988 and subjects (orphans, magicians, voyages, humorous stories). Plot beyond that unverified.
the-magic-hat-of-mortimer-wintergreen.summary: A humorous fantasy about a young orphan and a magician's magic hat, involving travel and magic. Plot details were not found beyond catalog subjects.
the-magic-hat-of-mortimer-wintergreen.title: The Magic Hat of Mortimer Wintergreen

characters: Janna — old woman in the forest
the-magic-stone.note: Dutch original De heksensteen (1974); English edition by Morrow, 1978, translated by Richard and Clara Winston. Draft guess of Dutch title 'De toverkei' not supported. The 'published' year is the Dutch original.
the-magic-stone.summary: Chris, a mischievous boy, finds a magic stone and learns that his friend's grandmother is a witch. The sorcerers' secret association wants the stone back.
the-magic-stone.title: The Magic Stone

the-magician-s-nephew.setting: London 1900 and the creation of Narnia
the-magician-s-nephew.summary: Digory and Polly are tricked into magic rings that carry them between worlds. They witness a dying world and the birth of Narnia, and learn where the wardrobe and the lamp-post came from.
the-magician-s-nephew.title: The Magician's Nephew

characters: The Marsh King's daughter — girl with two natures
The Marsh King — ruler of the bog
the-marsh-king-s-daughter.summary: A girl born to a stork-borne Egyptian princess and the Marsh King is raised by humans and divided between her good and wild nature. A long, haunting story from Hans Christian Andersen.
the-marsh-king-s-daughter.title: The Marsh King's Daughter

the-marvelous-misadventures-of-sebastian.summary: Sebastian, a talented young fiddler, is dismissed by a baron and sets out into a strange world of princes, pirates and magicians. With a runaway princess and a cat named Presto he finds music and danger go hand in hand.
the-marvelous-misadventures-of-sebastian.title: The Marvelous Misadventures of Sebastian

the-master-puppeteer.summary: Jiro, an apprentice at a puppet theater in eighteenth-century Osaka, uncovers a series of troubling mysteries. Hunger and poverty shape his world.
the-master-puppeteer.title: The Master Puppeteer

the-matchlock-gun.summary: During the French and Indian War, young Edward is left in charge of his mother and sister and the family's heavy old gun when raiders threaten.
the-matchlock-gun.title: The Matchlock Gun

characters: The Mennym family — life-size rag dolls living as humans
the-mennyms.note: Julia MacRae, 1993. The Wikipedia infobox dates the Guardian prize 1994; some of the page's smaller awards are marked 'citation needed'. Individual character names not verified.
the-mennyms.summary: The Mennyms are a family of life-size rag dolls who live quietly in England as an ordinary household. A letter from Australia threatens to expose the secret they have kept for decades.
the-mennyms.title: The Mennyms

the-midnight-horse.summary: Touch, an orphan, goes to live with his great-uncle in a crooked Vermont town. He and a ghostly magician help foil a scheme to take his inheritance.
the-midnight-horse.title: The Midnight Horse

the-midwife-s-apprentice.summary: A homeless girl called Brat is taken in by a sharp-tongued midwife. Slowly she gets a name, a home and a purpose.
the-midwife-s-apprentice.title: The Midwife's Apprentice

the-moffats.summary: Four Moffat children and their widowed mother live in a small Connecticut town, getting into small adventures that feel big. Warm, funny episodes of everyday childhood.
the-moffats.title: The Moffats

the-moon-is-down.setting: Occupied northern European town, World War II
the-moon-is-down.summary: An invading army occupies a small coastal town in a northern European country. The townspeople find quiet and stubborn ways to resist.
the-moon-is-down.title: The Moon Is Down

the-mouse-and-the-motorcycle.summary: Ralph, a mouse living in a seedy hotel, makes friends with a boy named Keith and learns to ride his toy motorcycle. Speed, adventure and a little trouble follow.
the-mouse-and-the-motorcycle.title: The Mouse and the Motorcycle

characters: Caroline Fish Carillon — the searching wife
Tony and Tina — her adopted twins
the-mysterious-disappearance-of-leon-i-m.note: Corrected: the heroine is Caroline Fish Carillon, not Ellen. Dutton, 1971; illustrator not confirmed.
the-mysterious-disappearance-of-leon-i-m.summary: Caroline Fish Carillon searches for her husband Leon, who now goes by Noel and vanished after shouting a garbled message while falling overboard from a boat. She spends years decoding it with her adopted twins and an old friend, in a story packed with word puzzles.
the-mysterious-disappearance-of-leon-i-m.title: The Mysterious Disappearance of Leon (I Mean Noel)

the-mystery-of-the-cupboard.summary: Omri discovers the surprising history of the cupboard and its key. The magic leads back through generations of his family.
the-mystery-of-the-cupboard.title: The Mystery of the Cupboard

characters: The Childlike Empress — ruler of Fantastica
the-neverending-story.note: German original Die unendliche Geschichte (Thienemann, 1979); English translation by Ralph Manheim, 1983.
the-neverending-story.summary: A lonely boy reads a stolen book about the magical land Fantastica, which is being swallowed by the Nothing. The boy becomes part of the tale, and each wish he makes costs him a memory.
the-neverending-story.title: The Neverending Story

the-night-daddy.note: Swedish original Nattpappan 1968; English translation by Gerry Bothmer, Delacorte 1971 (Open Library dates the work 1971). Plot from a bookseller snippet.
the-night-daddy.summary: A night-shift nurse hires a young writer to babysit her daughter. The girl comes to call him her "Night Daddy".
the-night-daddy.title: The Night Daddy

the-night-journey.note: Award year corrected to 1982; added illustrator; Association of Jewish Libraries Award from catalog snippet.
the-night-journey.setting: Mykolaiv in the Russian Empire, early 1900s; later Minnesota
the-night-journey.summary: Rachel overhears her great-grandmother Nana Sashie telling of her childhood escape from Russia. The story recounts flight from pogroms in the Russian Empire.
the-night-journey.title: The Night Journey

the-night-watchmen.note: Open Library subjects: Fantasy, Tramps, mystery. Wikipedia on Cresswell says it won the Phoenix Award in 1989. Illustrator Gareth Floyd could not be confirmed.
the-night-watchmen.summary: A children's fantasy by Helen Cresswell about tramps who act as night watchmen. First published by Macmillan in 1969.
the-night-watchmen.title: The Night-Watchmen

the-not-just-anybody-family.note: Delacorte, 1986. Draft said #2; it is the first Blossom Family book.
the-not-just-anybody-family.summary: Junior Blossom breaks both legs trying to fly off a barn roof, and his grandfather Pap lands in jail. Their widowed mother is away on the rodeo circuit, so Maggie and Vern work to rescue them.
the-not-just-anybody-family.title: The Not-Just-Anybody Family

the-old-curiosity-shop.illustrator: George Cattermole and Hablot K. Browne
the-old-curiosity-shop.summary: Young Nell Trent and her grandfather flee a cruel moneylender and wander across England. The dwarf Quilp pursues them.
the-old-curiosity-shop.title: The Old Curiosity Shop

the-old-man-and-the-sea.summary: Santiago, an aging Cuban fisherman, hooks an enormous marlin and battles it for days far out in the Gulf Stream. A spare story of endurance and dignity.
